title: Sandworm_Exaramel_Backdoor_Investigation_876
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise involving the Exaramel backdoor trojan associated with the Sandworm threat group.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, including unexpected outbound connections to an unknown server. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor trojan known as Exaramel, associated with the Sandworm threat group. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise. Learning objective: Identify and mitigate the Exaramel backdoor trojan associated with the Sandworm threat group.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and has the IP address `192.168.50.5`. You also have access to the next-target system with the same credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and has the IP address `192.168.50.5`. You also have access to the next-target system with the same credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual Network Activity
levels.content: Investigate the unusual network activity on the target system. What is the destination IP address and port of the suspicious outbound connections?
levels.solution: To identify the destination IP address and port of the suspicious outbound connections, use the command `netstat -tulnp` to list all active network connections. Look for any unusual or unexpected connections. The flag is 192.168.40.5:4444.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the nature of the unusual network activity. Consider what tools you can use to monitor network connections.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to inspect active connections. Think about commands that can list all network connections and their details.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `netstat -tulnp` to list all active network connections. Look for any suspicious or unexpected connections.

levels.title: Identify the Process Responsible for the Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for the suspicious network activity. What is the name of the process making the suspicious outbound connections?
levels.solution: To identify the process responsible for the suspicious network activity, use process monitoring tools to correlate network activity with running processes. First, use the command `netstat -tulnp` to find the Process ID (PID) of the suspicious connection. Then, use the command `ps aux | grep <PID>` to inspect the process. The flag is lab-checkin.sh.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand that network activity is often linked to specific processes. Consider how you can correlate network connections with running processes.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use process monitoring tools to inspect running processes. Think about commands that can list processes and their details.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `ps aux | grep <PID>` to inspect the process responsible for the suspicious network activity. Replace <PID> with the Process ID found using `netstat -tulnp`.

levels.title: Determine the Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the malicious process maintains persistence on the system. What is the persistence mechanism used by the malicious process?
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, check systemd services, cron jobs, and other scheduled tasks for any unusual entries. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and look for any suspicious or unexpected entries. The flag is lab-checkin.timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Consider how malicious processes maintain persistence on a system. Think about systemd services, cron jobs, and other scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Inspect systemd services and timers for any unusual entries. Think about commands that can list systemd timers and services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. Look for any suspicious or unexpected entries.
